rationale: Independent lead in the same recovery path: the startup replay of restoreFromCommittedLogs hands FSM batches to a buffered channel whose only consumer is started at the end of NewRaft, and the send has no timeout. This batch registers the new sourced question, the three behaviors behind it, and one fixed experiment that restarts prefixes whose committed log is far above their snapshot, with the flag on and off.

investigations.question: Can the startup replay that Config.RestoreCommittedLogs performs fail to complete? restoreFromCommittedLogs applies committed entries through processLogs before NewRaft starts the FSM goroutine, and processLogs hands each batch to a fixed-capacity channel, so the completion of NewRaft may depend on how much committed log lies above the snapshot.
investigations.hypothesis: processLogs sends each batch of at most MaxAppendEntries commit tuples to fsmMutateCh, a buffered channel created with capacity 128 whose only consumer is runFSM, started only after restoreFromCommittedLogs returns, and the send blocks until buffer space appears or shutdownCh closes. A replay containing more than 128 batches therefore blocks inside NewRaft, before the consumer exists and before any goroutine that could report an error runs; since NewRaft has not returned, no caller can close shutdownCh, so the send is not merely slow but unrepairable from within the process. The number of batches is ceil((commitIndex - lastApplied)/MaxAppendEntries), and at startup with the flag on lastApplied is the restored snapshot index, so the trigger is a committed log more than 128*MaxAppendEntries above the snapshot: 8192 entries with the default MaxAppendEntries of 64, which is the same order as the default SnapshotThreshold of 8192, and proportionally less with any smaller legal MaxAppendEntries.
investigations.discriminator: Build prefixes whose committed log lies far above an absent snapshot, then restart them with RestoreCommittedLogs on and off. If the replay volume alone were the problem, both restarts would stall or both would finish; if the ordering of the replay against the FSM consumer is the problem, only the flag-on restart fails to return, and a stack sample of the blocked goroutine names the replay frames.

knowledge.statement: processLogs applies committed entries in batches of at most config.MaxAppendEntries and delivers each batch with a select whose only cases are a send on r.fsmMutateCh and a receive on r.shutdownCh; when the channel has no free slot and the node is not shutting down, the send waits indefinitely.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to every caller of processLogs, including the startup replay in restoreFromCommittedLogs and the leader and follower apply paths (raft.go:1296-1364).

knowledge.statement: fsmMutateCh is created with capacity 128 in NewRaft's struct literal, and its consumer runFSM is started with r.goFunc(r.runFSM) only after restoreSnapshot, restoreFromCommittedLogs and the configuration scan have all returned; nothing else consumes fsmMutateCh.
knowledge.conditions: During NewRaft the channel has no consumer at all, so a replay requiring more than 128 batch sends cannot make progress (api.go:555-562, 628-640).

knowledge.statement: shouldSnapshot triggers when the log's last index minus the last snapshot index reaches config.SnapshotThreshold (default 8192, with MaxAppendEntries default 64 and SnapshotInterval default 120s), so the automatic snapshot cadence normally keeps the committed range above the snapshot near that threshold, and a store that keeps its log without snapshotting is not bounded by it.
knowledge.conditions: The threshold compares the log store's last index with the last snapshot index, not the applied index; it is a Config field (snapshot.go:107-121, config.go:331-342).

interpretations.rationale: Source trace. With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs set, NewRaft reads the persisted commit index and calls processLogs with it (api.go:723-754). processLogs walks from lastApplied+1 to that index, accumulating commit tuples and flushing a batch whenever the batch reaches config.MaxAppendEntries, delivering each batch through a select that waits for r.fsmMutateCh or r.shutdownCh (raft.go:1302-1312, 1336-1350). fsmMutateCh is created with capacity 128 (api.go:560) and is consumed only by runFSM, which NewRaft starts after the replay returns (api.go:636-638). At startup lastApplied is the restored snapshot index, so the replay spans the committed log above the snapshot, and the number of sends is ceil((commitIndex - lastApplied)/MaxAppendEntries). With the default MaxAppendEntries of 64 that is 128 sends at 8192 entries, so any restart whose committed range above the snapshot exceeds 8192 entries blocks inside NewRaft on the 129th send, with the FSM goroutine not yet started, no timeout, and no reachable way to close shutdownCh because the caller has not received the Raft object. The trigger is a legal configuration or workload: a smaller positive MaxAppendEntries lowers the bound proportionally, and a node that has never snapshotted (or whose snapshots lag its write rate) exceeds the default bound without any tuning. The failure is a startup liveness failure, not a wrong decision: the node never begins participating, so a single-voter group stays down and a larger group loses one member permanently. No repair is enabled in the blocked state: the only escape from the send is a shutdown channel that only a caller holding the returned object could close.
counterevidence: The default SnapshotThreshold of 8192 keeps the replay range near the 8192-entry bound rather than far above it, so on a fully auto-snapshotting node the block needs the range to overshoot the bound, for example because more entries were appended between the snapshot trigger and the snapshot completion. The claim does not rest on the default configuration alone: SnapshotThreshold and MaxAppendEntries are both legal config fields, and a store that keeps its log without snapshots reaches any range.

The existing feature test (raft_test.go:1183-1270) restarts with a log of about a hundred entries, far below the bound, so its passing result is not counterevidence to a bound that begins around 8192 default entries.
limitations: The receipt for this question's fixed experiment is not yet part of this account; a native local run of the same harness was used only to validate the operands during construction and is not offered as evidence.

The harness restarts a single-voter in-memory cluster with SnapshotThreshold raised so that no automatic snapshot is taken; it does not exercise a lowered MaxAppendEntries, an overshooting auto-snapshot, or a multi-node member loss.

The blocked state is reported as non-return within a fixed window plus a stack sample of the blocked goroutine; the permanence argument comes from the source, since nothing consumes the channel before runFSM starts.

scope.description: Build single-voter prefixes whose committed log lies about 9000 entries above an absent snapshot, then restart each prefix with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs on and off, calling NewRaft in a goroutine and reporting whether it returned within 8000ms together with a stack sample of the blocked goroutine.
assumptions: The prefix runs with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a raised SnapshotThreshold so the commit index is staged into the commit-tracking log store and no automatic snapshot moves the replay bound.
The restarted node keeps the same address and ID as its prefix and uses a fresh in-memory MockFSM, so the whole committed log above the snapshot is replayed.
The observation window of 8000ms is used only to decide completion; the claim that the block persists comes from the source, since the channel's consumer is started only after the replay returns.
excluded: No lowered MaxAppendEntries case, so the proportional relation between the bound and MaxAppendEntries is source-derived and not measured.
No multi-node cluster, so member loss caused by a node that cannot start is not measured.
No production log store, and no store whose StageCommitIndex is atomic with StoreLogs.

experiment.prefix: For each case, the harness builds its own prefix: NewInmemTransport with a random address, inmemConfig with LocalID = 'server-' + address, RestoreCommittedLogs true, SnapshotThreshold 1<<30 and SnapshotInterval one hour, plus NewInmemCommitTrackingStore, NewInmemStore and NewInmemSnapshotStore; BootstrapCluster with one Voter; NewRaft with a fresh MockFSM; wait for real leadership; then 9000 Apply calls, each waiting for its future. It records the store's commit index, last index, snapshot index and the computed batch count, then Shutdown. The case creates a new transport on the same address, copies the config with RestoreCommittedLogs set to the case value, and calls NewRaft in a separate goroutine. The main goroutine waits up to 8000ms for that call to return; if it does not, it samples all goroutine stacks with runtime.Stack and reports the excerpt around the first frame naming restoreFromCommittedLogs. If NewRaft returns, the harness waits up to one second for leadership, reports the state and then shuts the node down.
experiment.responsibility: NewRaft owns completion of its own startup work, including the RestoreCommittedLogs replay it performs before returning; the caller cannot observe or interrupt a NewRaft call that has not returned, so any unbounded wait in that path is owned by the library.

comparisons.description: NewRaft must return for a node whose stores hold a committed log; a restart that replays more than the FSM channel can hold must not leave NewRaft waiting forever.
Control: the same prefix shape restarted with the replay disabled returns from NewRaft, which distinguishes the replay path from a property of the prefix.
